sentences.text: Court No. - 27
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 5150 of 2023

Applicant :- Sachin Kumar Pandey
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Arvind Kumar Shukla,Supriya Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Brij Raj Singh,J.
1.

Heard Ms. Supriya Singh, learned counsel for the applicant as well as Shri Ravish Chandra
Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. This bail application has been filed seeking release of the accused/applicant Sachin Kumar
Pandey on bail, who is involved in Case Crime No. 0224 of 2022 under Sections 376-D, 354, 452,
504, 506 I.P.C, Police Station Kadipur, District Sultanpur.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the First Information Report was lodged by the father of the prosecutrix under Sections 452, 354, 504 and 506 I.P.C on 26.05.2022 in which allegation of molestation has been levelled against the applicant and other co-accused and no allegation of rape was levelled at that time in the F.I.R.

Thereafter, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. on 21.06.2022 i.e after 25 days from the date of incident wherein the prosecutrix had improved her version and has levelled allegation of rape against the Sachin Kumar Pandey vs State Of U.P. sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant has further stated that the medical examination of the prosecutrix was conducted on 11.11.2022, which was much belated, and the same is also not supporting the prosecution case.
As per medical report, the age of the prosecutrix is 19 years.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant further submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and the version of the First Information Report and the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C is contradictory to each other.

Learned counsel for applicant further stated that there is previous criminal history of 3 cases against the applicant which has been satisfactorily explained by her in the rejoinder affidavit and she further stated that the applicant is languishing in jail since 23.02.2023.

5. Learned A.G.A has opposed the prayer of bail of the applicant and has submitted that statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C indicates that the applicant committed rape on her, therefore, the applicant does not deserve mercy of the Court, thus his bail is liable to be rejected.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record, considering the nature of allegations, arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties, the argument that there is change of version in the F.I.R and the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C,
the argument that the prosecution case is highly doubtful, the fact that the medical report of the prosecutrix is not supporting the prosecution case, I find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
7. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Sachin Kumar Pandey be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
